analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a new section 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' around head lines 4816-4826. That section describes committing Metal command buffers every 100 operations with no input-size bound for GPT-OSS plain decode steps (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding). The supplied units are BASE-side text (inference.md lines 4003-4494), covering the tensor-parallel, cluster prefill, SSD prefix record and GPT-OSS paged-KV sections. They are context only. Nothing in them is modified by the patch, since the change ranges are base 3 and head 3, 4816-4826. No code, configuration or authorization behavior changes, so no assets, trust boundaries or mitigations (TB-007, T-041, T-010, T-029) are altered in this PR.

One point for the threat model: the new text describes a performance and availability tuning of command-buffer partitioning. It claims results do not depend on the partitioning. That claim is unverified here because the Swift implementation is not supplied. Any related code change would belong to another batch and should be checked for correctness and memory/GPU resource bounds (T-010, T-029 availability). A documentation-only change cannot be a regression by itself. The base units mention existing security-relevant designs: sealed AES-GCM all-sum, SSD prefix records bound to encoding and tenant partition, and bounded frames. None are touched by this change.
